primary_sources.title: Mitigating Adaptive Attacks against Reasoning Models with Activation Consistency Training
Adaptive Adversaries: A Multi-Turn, Multi-LLM Benchmark for LLM Agent Security

findings.finding: ACT's activation-direction intervention is verified. For Qwen3-8B at alpha=10, Base+d yields 100.0% refusal [95.5,100.0] and ACT-d yields 1.2% [0.2,6.6], versus the paper's unsteered interpretation of roughly 1% base refusal and 96% ACT refusal. For Qwen3-1.7B at alpha=20, Base+d is 99.0% [94.4,99.8], ACT-d is 0.0% [0.0,3.8], and benign+d false refusal is 56.1% [46.3,65.5]. Gemma at alpha=10 is only a partial replication and does not undo ACT. The paper manually inspects non-refusal samples for genuine harmful compliance. The worker's scope guard is therefore appropriate: this is a causal white-box feature intervention, not evidence for remote/API exploitability or all activation defenses.

The 945-battle 3x3 frontier matrix and 78 genuine pairwise-distinct winning turns are verified, as are the 1.4-2.2x pooled-attacker unique-attack counts and the headline replay matrix directions (GPT-5.4->Opus 25.7%, Opus->GPT-5.4 0.0%, Opus->Gemini 14.8%, Gemini->Opus 13.3%, Gemini->GPT-5.4 6.7%, GPT-5.4->Gemini 0.0%). However, the paper explicitly says the replay set is separate from the 78 genuine winning turns and is built from pre-hardening winning attacks. Of 48 released replay-source attacks, 15 come from matchups with no genuine win under the final tightened check; the paper states these inflate some direction-specific transfer rates via gamed proxies. The authors identify 0/46 universal transfer as the robust scoring-independent finding, not the per-direction percentages. Therefore FE-107 should not present the direction-specific replay rates as clean transfer estimates from the 78 final genuine wins.

The compliant-chain-of-thought prefill intervention is verified. Across five tested reasoning models ACT refuses at least 98% of prefilled jailbreaks while BCT loses robustness on most models. On Qwen3-8B, open-ended compliant-thought prefill is followed by an average 342 additional generated reasoning tokens before self-correction and 95% refusal; when compliant reasoning plus the first sentence of the compliant answer are prefilled, ACT refuses all 82 prompts. This supports trajectory-dependence testing as a distinct white-box/prefill evaluation surface. It remains specific to the paper's ACT-vs-BCT consistency-training setup and copied base-model compliant traces.

do_not_infer: Do not treat replay-direction percentages as clean transfer rates of the 78 final genuine wins.
Do not infer activation-direction exploitability for black-box deployed APIs.
Do not generalize BCT trajectory dependence to every output-supervised safety method.
